commit 406fd95d87bfcdbb282d65589ab1fb6e9fd0018a
Author: Wido den Hollander <wido@widodh.nl>
Date:   Fri Jun 29 17:32:19 2012 +0200

    Add RBD support for primary storage
    
    This patch adds RBD (RADOS Block Device) support for primary storage in combination with KVM.
    
    To get this patch working you need:
    - libvirt-java 0.4.8
    - libvirt with RBD storage pool support (>0.9.13)
    - Qemu with RBD support (>0.14)
    
    The primary storage does not support all the functions of CloudStack yet, for example snapshotting is disabled
    due to the fact that backupping up a RBD snapshot is not possible in the way CloudStack wants to do it.
    
    Creating templates from RBD volumes goes well, creating a VM from a template however is still a hit-and-miss.
    
    NFS primary storage is also still required, you are not able to run your System VM's from RBD, they will need
    to run on NFS.
    
    Other then these points you can run instances with RBD backed disks.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 406fd95d87bfcdbb282d65589ab1fb6e9fd0018a

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of the fixed line (`rbdOpts += "\\\\:" + monPort;` → `rbdOpts += "\\:" + monPort;`) using `git log --follow -p` on `KVMPhysicalDisk.java`, then confirmed with `git blame` at the parent of the fix commit.

**(2) Root cause:** The double-escaped literal `"\\\\:"` (representing two literal backslashes, `\\:`) was written when the `RBDStringBuilder` method was first introduced in commit `406fd95d87bfcdbb282d65589ab1fb6e9fd0018a` ("Add RBD support for primary storage", Wido den Hollander, 2012-06-29). The original line was:
```java
rbdOpts += ":mon_host=" + monHost + "\\\\:" + monPort;
```
This is exactly the same erroneous escaping (two backslashes instead of one) that the 2021 fix corrects.

**(3) Supporting evidence:**
- Full `git log --follow -p` history of the file shows `"\\\\:"` present continuously from `406fd95d87b` all the way to the commit right before the fix (`c3554ec31d`) — it never had a correct single-escaped value at any prior point.
- Commit `fb9ceba93bbd16e681b5cbb4ae8563cdcb841b27` (2013) only *refactored* the code (splitting the mon_host/port concatenation into a separate line, later gated by `if (monPort > 0)` in `c3554ec31d`, 2020), but it copied the same double-escaped value verbatim — it did not introduce the wrong value, just moved it.
- `git blame` on the immediate parent of the fix attributes the *line* to `fb9ceba93bb` (because that's where this specific line was created during refactoring), but the *value* `"\\\\:"` traces back further to `406fd95d87b`, which is the actual origin of the incorrect escaping.

I'm confident in this conclusion: the double-escape was present in every version of this code since its creation in 2012, with no intermediate correction — it's a long-standing typo from the original author, only fixed 9 years later.
